To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ingestion of fructose and protein together results in a similar insulin response to 50-g glucose, a similar glucagon response to fructose, a similar glucose response to fructose alone, and an additive insulin response to fructose and protein.
the ingestion of protein and fructose together results in an insulin response that is additive, but the glucose response is less than additive.
ingestion of 25 g fructosewith 25 g protein in subjects with type 1 diabetes results in a greater than expected response in insulin secretion but a less than expected response in glucose secretion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dietary protein on the regulation of glucose homeostasis in normal and diabetic subjects.
the regulation of the secretion of insulin and glucagon and the control of the plasma glucose concentration by nutrients.
the effects of dietary protein and fructose on glucose and insulin secretion in people with type II diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ingestion of protein and carbohydrate in combination stimulates insulin secretion in subjects with diabetes and that the insulin response is similar to that following the ingestion of an isoglycemic dose of glucose.
the ingestion of fructose and protein together results in an additive insulin response but a blunted glucose response.

ingestion of fructose with protein in people with untreated type 1 diabetes does not result in a significant increase in the insulin, glucagon or glucose response compared to ingestion of protein alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ingestion of 50 grams of protein with fructose is as good as ingesting 50 grams of glucose for stimulating insulin secretion in people with untreated type 1 diabetes.
ingestion of protein and fructose results in a similar insulin response as 50 g glucose, a response that is additive.
the ingestion of fructose in the presence of protein results in a greater than expected insulin response but a less than expected glucagon response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of protein to a fructose load results in an additive effect on insulin secretion, which is quantitatively equivalent to the response to an equal amount of carbohydrate.
protein, fructose and protein plus fructose all stimulate insulin secretion in a similar fashion.
the combination of fructose plus protein results in a similar insulin response to glucose.
